title: Abhishek's 69 and Arshdeep's Three-Fer Power India to 14-Run Win Over West Indies
excerpt: India defended 223 at Indore's Holkar Stadium to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match T20I series — the first successful defense by the team batting first on this tour.
body:
• India beat West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20I at Indore's Holkar Stadium on Sunday, taking a 2-1 lead in the five-match series.
  • Abhishek Sharma's 30-ball 69, studded with six fours and five sixes, powered India to 223 despite a middle-order collapse from 115 for 1 to 135 for 5.
  • Arshdeep Singh claimed 3 for 44, dismissing the in-form Shai Hope cheaply, while Naman Dhir's two wickets broke the chase in the middle overs.
  • It was the first time on this tour that the team batting first successfully defended a total — the previous two matches were both won by the chasing side.

A total finally defended

For the first time in a run-drenched series, batting first turned out to be the winning move. On an Indore pitch where low bounce made timing the ball genuinely hard, India's 223 all out proved just out of reach as the bowlers shut West Indies out at 209 for 7, closing the game out well before the final over with yorkers into a dry ball.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2109378732985290800

The result flips the series dynamic. West Indies had walked into Indore buoyed by Friday's record-equalling heroics in Ranchi, where they chased down 250 — the second-highest successful chase in T20 international history — to level the series. India needed an answer. Abhishek Sharma and Arshdeep Singh provided it at opposite ends of the game.

Abhishek's assault sets it up

Put in to bat after losing the toss, India got off to a rocky start when Sanju Samson fell for 3. What followed was a 108-run blitz for the second wicket between the two left-handers, Abhishek and Ishan Kishan. Abhishek reached his fifty off just 18 balls, and his 30-ball 69 was the only innings in the match to score at more than 14 runs an over.

West Indies fought back through spinner Roston Chase, who removed Kishan for 37 and captain Shreyas Iyer for 1 in the same over, and Shamar Springer, who cut short Abhishek's knock. From 115 for 1 in the 8.1 overs, India slid to 135 for 5. The middle order's wobble meant the finish relied on lower-order graft — Tilak Varma's 28, Nitish Kumar Reddy's 21, Axar Patel's 20, and an unbeaten 13 off six balls from Prince Yadav pushed the total to 223.

The chase that fell short

West Indies' chase lost its most dangerous weapon early. Shai Hope, unbeaten on 102 in Friday's record chase, fell cheaply to Arshdeep's new-ball strike. Shimron Hetmyer counter-attacked — dropped by Abhishek on 5, he made the reprieve count with a six and three fours in a 19-run fourth over — but his 43 off 26 balls ended when part-timer Naman Dhir skidded one through him. Dhir struck again to remove Kamil Pooran for 42, and with Sherfane Rutherford's 32 the only other score of note, the innings kept losing wickets at the wrong times.

A late 35 not out off 11 balls from Shamar Springer added respectability, but India had already done the damage. As ESPNcricinfo's report noted, take Abhishek's 14-runs-an-over innings out, and both sides scored at roughly 10 an over for the rest of the match.

Bowlers answer the call

The standout subplot was India's bowling redemption. Axar Patel, smashed for 63 runs in 3.3 wicketless overs at Ranchi, stalled West Indies through the middle overs this time. The absence of dew — which had tilted the first two games toward the chasers — let the spinners grip the ball, and Arshdeep's pinpoint death bowling kept India just out of reach throughout.

"It was wonderful to see the bowlers being confident. The clarity was very much visible when I was interacting. They were ready to take up the challenge and that's what we want."

— Shreyas Iyer, India captain

West Indies skipper Shai Hope was candid about the margins: "Probably with the ball, we could've executed a little bit better. So those little margins would be the deciding factor come the end of the game."

Diaspora angle

India now need only one win from the final two matches to seal the series — and the turnaround story of Axar Patel, written off after Ranchi and reborn in Indore, is the kind of arc that travels well with every fan who's followed this team through a season of close finishes.

What's next

The fourth T20I is now the series' pivotal game: a win gives India the series with a match to spare, while West Indies must win to force a decider. The visitors will want to rethink their death bowling, which leaked the 15-odd runs that ultimately decided this match. For full ball-by-ball detail, see the ESPNcricinfo match report.
